passage:
On the veranda of the farmhouse, Kamal held his slate up with both hands. “Look, Amma! A buffalo!” Rukmini wiped her wet hands on her sari and bent down. The buffalo had four uneven legs and one enormous eye. “Ah, you made the horns curl. And the tail swings.”
Kamal's chest puffed out. “I did the tail three times.”
“Three times! You kept trying.”
“Now you do a hen.”
Rukmini laughed. “I will do a very bad hen.” They sat down together on the step.

qa.q: How many times did Kamal do the tail?
qa.a: He said he did the tail three times.

qa.q: How can you tell Kamal felt proud, and what else might it show?
qa.a: His chest puffed out, he held the slate up with both hands and told her about the tail. It might also show he wanted her attention while she was busy.

qa.q: What kind of praise helped here, and why?
qa.a: Rukmini noticed specific effort, the curled horns and the repeated tail, instead of saying “best ever”, so Kamal's pride is tied to his own trying. 🙂

qa.q: What might Rukmini be feeling as she wipes her hands and bends down?
qa.a: Probably warmth and delight, since she stopped what she was doing to look. She might also be busy or tired but chose to give him her attention.

grounding: A preschooler says look with a drawing; pride grows with attention to real effort.

passage:
By the cubbies, Santiago sat on the floor with his sneaker in his lap, tongue between his teeth, looping the lace the way Mr Kofi had shown the group. It took a long time, and the other children were already outside. At last he pulled, and the bow sat slightly crooked on his foot. He jumped up. “Mr Kofi! Look, look!”
Mr Kofi crouched. “You tied it yourself. I watched you work on it.”
“I did the loop and the other loop.”
“You did.”
Santiago grinned. “Now the other one.”

qa.q: Which teacher did Santiago show his shoe to?
qa.a: He showed it to Mr Kofi.

qa.q: What was Santiago feeling when he grinned and asked to do the other shoe?
qa.a: Proud and pleased with his effort, and keen to keep going. He could also simply be enjoying Mr Kofi's attention.

qa.q: What would you advise a teacher to say to a child showing a tied shoe?
qa.a: Notice the real effort, as Mr Kofi did with “I watched you work on it”, and share the delight without heavy praise.

qa.q: How might Mr Kofi see the crooked bow?
qa.a: As the result of Santiago's real work rather than a mistake to fix, since he praised what he watched the boy do and not how neat the bow was.

grounding: A preschooler holds up a tied shoe and says look; shared delight in real effort.
